feature: A screen's columns start where its padding does
summary: Give a screen room at its edges and its columns are now drawn inside that room, on all four sides, so a box the screen lays out at its padding begins exactly on the first column. The Columns section no longer offers a Margin of its own on a screen that has padding, because the padding is the one inset it has.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on: frames and arranging both come on already.

try.do: Draw a screen with the frame tool, about 800 by 600.
Draw a rectangle inside it, anywhere.
Click the empty part of the screen to pick the screen itself, then press Shift Command S so it arranges its contents.
In Layout, type 12 into Padding and press Return. The rectangle moves in to 12.
Look along the top left corner: the first column and the rectangle start on the same line, across and down.
Type 40 into Padding. The columns move with it, and there is no second number to update.
Open Each side under Padding and set Left back to 12: the columns follow each side on its own.

evaluate: With padding of 12, does the first column look like it starts exactly where the rectangle does, or can you still see daylight between them?
Now that the columns are inset from the top and bottom too, do they read as the screen's layout, or did the full height version tell you more?
Losing the Margin field on a padded screen: does the sentence that replaces it tell you enough about where the columns come from, or do you want to type the number here as well as in Layout?
On a screen with no padding the Margin field is still there. Is that a helpful leftover or a second number you would rather not see at all?
Does the red wash reading over the rectangle rather than behind it make the alignment harder to judge?
rough: Margin is kept, not retired. On a screen that keeps no room at its edges the columns still use it, and the field is still in the Columns section; the moment the screen has padding the field goes away and a sentence takes its place. That choice is what keeps every document anybody has already saved drawing its columns exactly where it drew them yesterday: nothing is migrated, nothing moves, and a screen that wants columns hard against its edges can still have them by typing 0 into Margin.

The Layout section shows a Padding number for a screen that was never given a layout, read off where its contents already sit. The columns do NOT follow that one, because guides that jump when you drag a rectangle would be worse than guides that wait. So a screen you have never arranged can show Padding 40 in Layout while its columns sit on their own margin. Typing anything into Padding settles it. Worth watching for a report.

The bands are drawn over the screen and its contents, so the rectangle under the first column reads a shade pinker than it is. That is how the overlay has always drawn and it is deliberate, but it is most noticeable exactly where you are now looking, at a box that lines up with a column.
